citations.title: Patient rights
citations.requirement: The governing authority must adopt written patient-rights policies and procedures. Patients get their rights in writing before care starts, with documentation in the clinical record (a)(1). They get a statement of services and charges (a)(2). They are told before care how much third-party payers are expected to pay and how much the patient must pay (a)(3). Any change must be given within 30 calendar days of the agency learning of it, orally and in writing (a)(3)(i)-(ii). Other rights: be told what services will be provided and by whom (a)(4); take part in care planning (a)(5); refuse care (a)(6); complain free of reprisal (a)(7)-(9); be treated with respect (a)(10); privacy of records (a)(11); refuse advanced home health aide tasks (a)(12). Agencies must tell patients they may complain to the DOH Office of Health Systems Management (a)(9). All care staff must know these rights (b). A legally authorized representative exercises the rights if the patient lacks capacity (c).

citations.title: Patient service policies and procedures
citations.requirement: Each service needs written policies and procedures, reviewed and revised as necessary (a)(1). Service delivery is documented in the clinical record (a)(2). Continuity: the same personnel serve the same patient where possible (a)(3). Caregivers carry current ID showing name, title, photo and agency name, returned on separation (a)(4). Written procedures cover storage, cleaning and disinfection of supplies and equipment (a)(5). Any new nursing or therapeutic service must go to the QI committee first (a)(7). A discharge plan starts before discharge (a)(8). Discharge happens only after notice to the authorized practitioner and consultation with the patient and staff, at least 48 hours before discharge (a)(9). "Health care services" are defined in (b) and include personal care.

citations.title: Plan of care
citations.requirement: A patient is accepted only after an RN, or a person directly supervised by an RN, determines the agency can safely and adequately meet the patient's needs (a). A plan of care is built on a professional assessment (b). It covers diagnosis, prognosis, mental status, frequency of each service, medications, treatments, diet, functional limitations and rehabilitation potential. The plan is reviewed and revised as often as needed, and at least every six months, with each review documented in the clinical record (d)(1). Staff promptly alert the authorized practitioner and other affected providers to significant changes in condition (d)(2).

citations.title: Medical orders
citations.requirement: Section 766.4 exists in Part 766 (title confirmed from the Part 766 table of contents). The text was not retrieved. §766.2(a)(9) refers to 766.4(b) for the definition of "authorized practitioner". Confirm the full text before quoting in the manual.

citations.title: Clinical supervision
citations.requirement: The governing authority must ensure sufficient trained supervisory staff (a). Supervision includes case review, in-home visits to direct and evaluate care, clinical consultation, and consultation on policy. Evidence of adequate supervision (b): services delivered at the planned times and frequencies; assignment by licensure, training and demonstrated skill; prompt charting and reporting of changes in condition, adverse reactions, and problems with informal supports or the home; plans revised as needed. Aides are supervised "as appropriate" by an RN (c). In-home professional supervision occurs (d): (1) at the initial service visit or on a change in personnel, if the aide lacks documented training and experience in the tasks, with return demonstration; (2) when a change in condition occurs, to evaluate and revise the plan; (3) to instruct the aide on required observations and written reports. Paragraph (e) covers advanced home health aides (RN home visit at least every two weeks). Not applicable unless the agency uses AHHAs.

citations.title: Patient care record
citations.requirement: Each patient has a confidential record (a) containing: identifying data; medical orders; nursing assessments; the plan of care; signed and dated progress notes after each visit or phone contact; RN supervisory reports; aide observations and activity sheets; documentation of accidents and incidents (a)(8); documentation that rights information was received (a)(9); and a discharge summary (a)(10). Records are kept securely at least 6 years after discharge and are available to DOH (b). For minors, keep until 6 years after discharge or 3 years after age 18, whichever is longer (c). If the agency closes, the governing authority must arrange storage and access and notify DOH in writing where records are kept (d). Written policies must safeguard records against loss or unauthorized access and govern use, removal and release (e).

citations.title: Governing authority
citations.requirement: The governing authority is responsible for operation and compliance with all laws (a)-(b). It must keep a current written emergency plan and orient all employees to it (c). It adopts and amends policies (d) and makes public its services, service area, charges and payment mechanisms (e). It provides an adequate office with access to patient records and prompt phone contact (f). It employs enough staff (g). It employs at least one licensed, registered RN to direct and supervise all patient care (h). It accepts only patients whose needs can be met under written criteria (i). The complaint procedure (j) requires a complaint log; a written response within 15 days; notice of the right to appeal; appeal review by a governing-authority member or committee within 30 days; and notice of the right to complain to DOH. A continuous QI program is required (k). A QI committee with a consumer and health professionals meets at least four times a year (l): it reviews policies; reviews a random sample of current patients' and past-3-month discharges' records plus all complaint cases; and sends a written summary to the governing authority. Management contracts (m) and franchise agreements (n) need prior written commissioner consent; submit proposals at least 60 days before the effective date. Subdivision (o): HPN accounts, 24/7 emergency contacts, a written HPN coverage policy reviewed at least annually, and directory updates at least monthly.

citations.title: Contracts
citations.requirement: The agency may contract for patient care services. Services by arrangement require a written contract (b). Contract personnel must meet §766.11 personnel requirements (c). The agency remains responsible for the adequacy of contracted services (d). Nurses or therapists under contract must coordinate and integrate with agency services (e). Subdivision (f) addresses personal care contracts with local social services districts. Only the opening text of this section was seen; confirm the full text.

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: Written personnel policies are reviewed at least annually (a). Aide qualifications under §700.2 must be met, and the PHL §3613(3)(a)-(f) information must be in the Home Care Registry (b). Health status is assessed before assuming duties (c). For personnel with direct patient contact (d): rubella immunity; measles immunity if born on or after 1/1/1957; TB risk assessment, symptom evaluation and TB test before employment and annually; an annual health status assessment; and influenza vaccination documentation or a mask during flu season. Identity is verified before hire (e). Employment history and references are verified before patient contact, and a criminal history record check is run as required by Part 402 (f). Personnel records hold verifications, licenses, evaluations and employment dates; health records are kept separate and confidential (g). Time and payment records are kept (h). Orientation is required, and in-service is at least 12 hours a year for HHAs, 6 for PCAs and 18 for AHHAs (i). Each position has a written job description (j). An annual performance assessment includes at least one in-home observation visit where applicable (k). A bloodborne-pathogen program (l) covers barriers, training at hire and yearly, PPE, monitoring, and an exposure-management procedure.

citations.title: Records and reports
citations.requirement: The agency must promptly submit all records and reports DOH requires (a). The principal NYS office keeps: the license, organizational documents, assumed-name certificate, patient-care contracts, governing-authority and QA bylaws, current policies, a current patient roster and a listing of all personnel (a)(1). Branch offices keep policies, a personnel list and patient records (a)(2). Retention minimums (a)(3): governing authority and committee minutes, 3 years; patient-care financial records, 3 years; personnel records, 3 years after separation; complaint and grievance records, 3 years after resolution; patient care records per §766.6. Electronic records must be secure, confidential and printable on request (b). Each year the agency furnishes DOH with statistical summaries of services and reimbursement, plus an ownership list (c).

citations.title: Definitions (home care services agency; licensed home care services agency; aide qualifications)
citations.requirement: Defines a home care services agency (a)(6) and a licensed home care services agency (a)(25) as one licensed under PHL Article 36. Per the fact-checked research, it also defines personal care aide and home health aide qualifications and training. The aide-definition text was past the truncation point in the fetch.

citations.title: Medicaid personal care services: scope, levels, minimum needs, assessment and authorization
citations.requirement: Personal care must be medically necessary, ordered by a qualified independent practitioner, based on assessment, delivered under a plan of care and supervised by an RN (a)(1). Eligibility requires a stable medical condition and self-direction, with the exceptions stated (a)(3)(i)-(ii). Minimum needs (a)(3)(iv): dementia or Alzheimer's needs supervision with more than one ADL; all others need limited assistance with physical maneuvering with more than two ADLs. Continuous PCS is more than 16 hours/day by more than one aide (a)(2). Live-in 24-hour PCS is one aide whose sleep is likely to be uninterrupted for 5 hours (a)(4). Level I covers nutritional and environmental support tasks only, authorized for no more than 8 hours/week (a)(5)(i). Level II adds personal care functions (a)(5)(ii)(a)(1)-(13), including medication prompting and assistance, but not administration (a)(5)(ii)(a)(10). Additional documentation is needed before authorizing more than 12 hours/day on average (a)(5)(ii)(b). Assessment (b): an independent RN assessment (RN licensed in NYS with 2+ years of home care experience), an independent medical exam and practitioner order, and plan development by the district or MMCO. Telehealth is allowed if an in-person option is offered.

citations.title: Personal care aide training and qualifications
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: a personal care aide for Medicaid needs a DOH-approved HHA program or the 40-hour PCA basic training, completed within 3 months of hire, plus 3 hours of in-service semiannually. Subdivision (e) text was not seen in the truncated fetch.

citations.title: Nursing supervision of personal care aides
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: an RN supervisory visit at least every 90 days, with a combined visit possible every six months for stable, self-directing clients. Later DOH rulemaking amended (f)(3)(vi) so the local district or MMCO determines the supervision frequency (regs.health.ny.gov summary of express terms). OMIG audit guidance says some counties require only six-month visits, so the frequency must be stated on the plan of care or in the contract. Keep a written report for each visit with the aide present. Confirm the current (f) text and the MLTC contract.

citations.title: Criminal history record check process
citations.requirement: Request a check for each prospective employee (a). An authorized person signs the DOH form, and the form and two sets of fingerprints go to DOH within 10 business days (excluding weekends and legal holidays) of taking the prints (b). The applicant presents two IDs, one government-issued with signature and at least one with photo (c)(1). Resubmit within 14 days of notice that prints were rejected (c)(3). Temporary approval is allowed pending results, with the §402.4 supervision (d). An expedited review request applies if the person has a prior determination or a pending submission (e).

citations.title: Home Care Worker Registry
citations.requirement: Part 403 applies to every Article 36 licensed agency. The agency must designate at least two individuals to access and enter data in the registry (§403.3(a)), and it must have policies implementing Part 403 (§403.3(b)). Only designated individuals may submit data (§403.3(c)). Within 10 business days after an aide begins providing services, the registry must be updated with employment information including the start date (§403.5(a)(6), as described in DOH DAL 19-21). A person trained in a state-approved program on or after 9/25/2009 may not provide services until posted to the registry (§403.5).

citations.title: Home care services workers (registry)
citations.requirement: Establishes the Home Care Services Worker Registry and the information entered for each worker who completes a state-approved training program (name, address, gender, date of birth, program). Also provides for indicating advanced home health aide status and any limitation or revocation of that status.

citations.title: Licensure of home care services agencies
citations.requirement: A license is required to provide nursing, home health aide or personal care services. PHHPC approval considers public need, character and competence, and financial resources. The application fee is $2,000 (subd. 13), per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Annual LHCSA registration
citations.requirement: Annual registration since 1/1/2019. Unregistered agencies may not operate or be paid. The late penalty is $500 per month, and missing two registration periods can lead to revocation.

citations.title: Home care worker wage parity
citations.requirement: For Medicaid-funded home care in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester: total compensation is the home care aide minimum plus a benefit portion of $2.54/hour (NYC) or $1.67/hour (Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester) from 1/1/2024. Requires an annual certification and an independently audited statement. Records are kept 10 years, per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Home care aide minimum wage
citations.requirement: Minimum wage for home care aides: $19.65 (NYC, Long Island, Westchester) and $18.65 (rest of state) as of 1/1/2026. This rises to $20.00 and $19.00 on 1/1/2027.

citations.title: Cost reporting
citations.requirement: Cost reports are filed when DOH requires them: within 90 days of notice, with a 30-day correction window (2018 amendments), per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Application review standards; determinations of public need
citations.requirement: Character, competence and financial feasibility standards, with working capital of at least two months of estimated operating expenses (§765-1.2). Public need rebuttable presumption of no need where 5 or more LHCSAs each actively serve 25+ patients in a county. Initial applicants must commit to serve hard-to-reach groups (§765-1.16(e)). Per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Influenza vaccination or mask for health care personnel
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced from §766.11(d)(6). The section text itself was not fetched. Confirm the current rule text before quoting in the manual.

citations.title: HIV/bloodborne pathogen definitions and exposure standards
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced from §766.11(l)(1) for the definition of significant-risk body substances. The section text itself was not fetched. Confirm before quoting.

citations.title: Medicaid provider compliance programs
citations.requirement: Medicaid providers that meet the statutory billing threshold must keep an effective compliance program. NOT retrieved or verified here; confirm applicability and the threshold with counsel or OMIG before adopting. The compliance policy should be written either way.

citations.cite: DOH MLTC Policy: LHCSA contract limits
citations.title: Licensed Home Care Services Agencies contract guidance
citations.requirement: MLTC plans may contract with no more than 1 LHCSA per 100 enrollees downstate or per 60 rest of state, with at least two LHCSAs per county accepting new enrollees. Exceptions: LHCSAExceptions@health.ny.gov. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.cite: DOH Electronic Visit Verification (21st Century Cures Act, 42 USC 1396b(l))
citations.title: EVV for Medicaid personal care
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care services from 1/1/2021 (choice model: the agency picks its own vendor), with data sent to the NYS EVV Data Aggregator. It captures date, location, service, people, and start and end times. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Minimum Needs Requirements effective 9/1/2025
citations.requirement: Adults 21+ seeking PCS or CDPAS must need limited assistance with more than two ADLs (more than one ADL with supervision for dementia or Alzheimer's). It applies to initial assessments and reassessments on or after 9/1/2025, and to Medicaid recipients 18+ seeking MLTC or MAP enrollment. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Weekly HERDS reporting by LHCSAs
citations.requirement: Weekly HERDS reporting includes patient census by licensed county. The window opens Tuesday 8:00 a.m. and closes Thursday 2:00 p.m. (since 6/17/2025). Contact hcstatrpts@health.ny.gov. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.cite: NYSDOH LHCSA Policy & Procedure Manual Review Tool (Part B)
citations.title: DOH review tool for LHCSA P&P manuals
citations.requirement: DOH reviewers check P&P manuals against 10 NYCRR 766 (including §766.11(b)-(c)) and Part 403 registry provisions. Use it as the surveyor's checklist.

citations.title: PCA/HHA/AHHA training documentation verification
citations.requirement: When hiring aides, review the available training materials to confirm training from a DOH- or SED-approved program. The materials must include the Home Care Registry aide profile; the training certificate is included if available.

citations.cite: OMIG Audit Protocol: Personal Care Aides (guidance, rev. 5/11/15)
citations.title: Personal care audit criteria
citations.requirement: Audit guidance only; it does not create legal requirements. It describes disallowance of claims where there is no documented RN supervisory visit within 120 days before the sampled date of service. A written report is needed for each visit. The visit frequency should appear on the plan of care or in the contract.

citations.cite: DOH Medicaid Managed Care NYIA guidance
citations.title: MMC guidance on NYIA, plan of care and authorizations
citations.requirement: The plan remains responsible for authorizing services and must record the level, amount, frequency and duration of authorized services in the plan of care, with notice to the enrollee. Plans coordinate with the NYIA on assessments and practitioner orders (18 NYCRR 505.14(b)(2)(iii)).

citations.title: P&P manual and pre-opening survey
citations.requirement: After PHHPC contingent approval, the P&P manual goes to the regional home care office. The regional office must accept it before the pre-opening survey. Per the fact-checked research.

policies.title: Governing Authority, Administrator and RN Director Responsibilities
state_specifics: The governing authority is responsible for operation and compliance with all laws (766.9(a)-(b)).
It adopts and amends all policies and adopts the budget.
It keeps a current written emergency plan and orients all employees to it (766.9(c)).
It provides an adequately sized office with access to patient records and prompt phone contact (766.9(f)).
It employs at least one licensed, registered RN to direct and supervise all patient care (766.9(h)).

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area, Public Information and Advertising
state_specifics: A license is required for nursing, home health aide or personal care services (PHL §3605).
Serve only the counties named on the license. Adding counties is a license amendment and is subject to the public-need rule.
Make public the services, service area, charges and accepted payers (agency brochure) (766.9(e)).
Annual registration is required under PHL §3605-b. The late penalty is $500/month, and missing two periods can lead to revocation.
Initial applicants commit to serve hard-to-reach groups (10 NYCRR 765-1.16(e)).

policies.title: Policy Manual Format, Index, Document Control and Required Program Materials
state_specifics: Every policy carries: agency name as on the PHHPC approval, discrete number, title, purpose, policy and revision dates, 'page x of y', authority, application, responsible party, terminology, cross-references.
Every policy has a step-by-step procedure: overview, skills and materials, logical sequence of steps, examples where useful.
The index lists policy name, number, initial/revision date and the regulation cited.
Keep a job description and a policy for each approved service: Nursing, Personal Care Aide and any other service PHHPC approved (e.g., Home Health Aide).

Submit the manual to the regional office after contingent approval. It must be accepted before the pre-opening survey. Policies are reviewed at least annually (766.11(a)) and revised as necessary (766.2(a)(1)).

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QI Committee)
state_specifics: A continuous QI program covers all staff and all services (766.9(k)).
The QI committee includes a consumer and health professionals and meets at least 4 times a year (766.9(l)).
Each meeting reviews policies, a random sample of current patients' records, records of patients discharged in the prior 3 months, and all complaint cases.
The committee sends a written summary of findings to the governing authority.
Any new nursing or therapeutic service goes to the QI committee first (766.2(a)(7)).

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Bill only for services delivered, authorized and documented (EVV record, aide activity sheet, RN supervisory report).
Medicaid compliance-program applicability under SSL §363-d/18 NYCRR Part 521 has not been verified. Confirm with counsel or OMIG; the policy is written either way.
Name a compliance officer, with training, a reporting hotline and a non-retaliation rule.
Cost reports are filed within 90 days of DOH notice, with a 30-day correction window (PHL §3612).
Overpayments are reported and returned. OMIG may disallow claims that lack a documented RN supervisory visit.

policies.title: Contracts and Services by Arrangement
state_specifics: Services by arrangement need a written contract (766.10(b)).
Each contract states the services, how they are supervised and evaluated, charges and financial arrangements, a 'notwithstanding' clause, and indemnification between agency and contractor.
Contract personnel must meet all 766.11 personnel requirements (766.10(c)).
The agency remains responsible for the adequacy of contracted services (766.10(d)).
Management and franchise contracts need prior written commissioner consent, submitted at least 60 days ahead (766.9(m)-(n)). Confirm the full text of 766.10.

policies.title: Health Commerce System (HCS) Account and Communication Directory
state_specifics: Obtain an HCS account for each agency operated (766.9(o)).
Access HCS daily, with coverage throughout operating hours and enough staff to answer DOH requests quickly.
Keep the 24/7 facility contact and Office of the Administrator current. Update the directory at least monthly.
The written HPN coverage policy is reviewed at least annually.

Assign these roles: Administrator; Director of Patient Services; Emergency Response Coordinator; HCS Coordinator; CHRC Authorized Person; Home Care Registry Updater and Viewer (at least two registry designees under Part 403).

policies.title: Change of Ownership, Transfer of Interests and Management Changes
state_specifics: A license is not transferable. A change of ownership needs a new application and PHHPC approval before it takes effect.
Define a change of ownership: transfer of interests, stock or membership interests, or acquisition of control.
Notify DOH before the change and file the application electronically (NYSE-CON).
Management contracts need commissioner approval 60 days ahead (766.9(m)).
Failure to disclose a change can void an approval.

policies.title: Amendment of the License (Counties, Services, Sites)
state_specifics: An amendment includes adding a county, adding a service or changing or adding a site or office location.
Obtain DOH approval before acting. Contact the regional office or homecareapplications@health.ny.gov.
Submit the application materials DOH requires for each type of amendment.
New counties are still subject to the public-need rule (10 NYCRR 765-1.16).
Update the P&P manual, the HCS directory and the agency brochure after each approved amendment.

policies.title: Patient Rights and Responsibilities (Notice, Documentation and Exercise of Rights)
state_specifics: Give rights in writing and explain them verbally before care starts. Document receipt in the clinical record (766.1(a)(1); 766.6(a)(9)).
Tell the patient what services will be provided, when and how, and the name, title and function of who will provide them. Give notice of any change in services or plan of care (766.1(a)(4)).
Patient rights: take part in care planning, refuse care, complain free of reprisal, dignity and respect, privacy and confidentiality of records, and refuse release of records to outside agencies.
Patients may complain to DOH. Include the DOH complaint hotline number on the rights notice.
A legally authorized representative exercises the rights if the patient lacks capacity (766.1(c)). All care staff are trained on the rights (766.1(b)).

policies.title: Service Agreement, Statement of Services, Charges and Payer Liability
state_specifics: Before care starts, give a written statement of services and charges (766.1(a)(2)).
Before care, tell the patient how much third-party payers (Medicaid, MLTC plans, insurance) are expected to pay and how much the patient must pay (766.1(a)(3)).
Give notice of any change in charges or coverage within 30 calendar days of the agency learning of it, orally and in writing (766.1(a)(3)(i)-(ii)).
Make charges and accepted payment sources public (766.9(e)).
The patient or representative signs the service agreement and the informed consent.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Keep a complaint log. Document receipt, investigation and resolution of every complaint (766.9(j)).
Give a written response to written complaints, and to oral complaints on request, within 15 days of the investigation findings.
Advise the complainant of the right to appeal. A governing-authority member or committee reviews the appeal and notifies the complainant within 30 days.

Advise the complainant of the right to complain to DOH. Print the DOH home care complaint hotline number on every notice; confirm the current number with DOH before printing (historically 1-800-628-5972).
Send all complaints to the QI committee. Retain complaint records 3 years after resolution (766.12(a)(3)).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Patients have the right to privacy and confidential treatment of their records (766.1(a)(11)).
Release records to outside parties only with patient authorization or as law permits, and tell the patient they may refuse release.
Electronic records must be secure and confidential (766.12(b)).
Provide a HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices.
Train all staff at hire and yearly. Report breaches under HIPAA.

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Caregivers may not accept gifts, loans, bequests or money from clients or families.
Caregivers may not handle client cash, cards or bank accounts beyond documented, authorized errands with receipts.
Caregivers may not borrow from clients or sell them anything, or use client property.
Caregivers report any suspected exploitation to the RN director immediately.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (42 USC 2000d)
state_specifics: Accept patients without discrimination on race, color, national origin, disability, age, sex, religion or payer source.
Provide interpreters and translated rights notices at no charge.
Make reasonable accommodations for disability.
Record the language preference in the intake record.

policies.title: Personal Care Aide Duties, Scope of Tasks and What Caregivers May and May Not Do
state_specifics: Level I covers nutritional and environmental support tasks only, authorized for no more than 8 hours a week (18 NYCRR 505.14(a)(5)(i)).
Level II adds personal care functions such as bathing, toileting, dressing and feeding, plus medication prompting and assistance but not administration (505.14(a)(5)(ii)).
Aides work only from the written plan of care and aide care plan, under an order from an authorized practitioner. The Medicaid order must come from a qualified independent practitioner.
Aides may not perform nursing tasks or injections.
Aides may refuse advanced home health aide tasks (766.1(a)(12)).

policies.title: Admission Criteria, Acceptance of Patients and Informed Consent
state_specifics: The governing authority sets written admission criteria (766.9(i)).
Accept a patient only after an RN, or a person directly supervised by an RN, determines the agency can safely and adequately meet the assessed needs (766.3(a)).
Accept patients without discrimination.
Obtain informed consent and give the rights notice and charges statement before the first service.
Decline or refer out when needs exceed agency capacity or staffing.

policies.title: Client Intake, Medicaid Eligibility, Independent Assessment and Minimum Needs
state_specifics: Medicaid personal care requires an independent RN assessment, an independent medical exam and a practitioner order. Plan development is by the district or the MLTC plan/MMCO (18 NYCRR 505.14(b)).
Minimum needs: for adults 21+, limited assistance with more than two ADLs, or more than one ADL with supervision for dementia/Alzheimer's.
Minimum needs apply to assessments and reassessments on or after 9/1/2025.
The plan authorizes level, amount, frequency and duration. Staff only to those hours.
Private-pay intake follows the RN assessment under SVC-05.

policies.title: Nursing Services (RN Responsibilities and Standards of Practice)
state_specifics: Nursing practice follows the NY Nurse Practice Act, scope of practice and standards of practice. The RN director directs and supervises all patient care (766.9(h)).
Nursing services require orders from an authorized practitioner.
Name who provides nursing services: the RN director or staff RNs.
The RN coordinates services with the practitioner, MLTC care manager and other providers. Hold clinical conferences and document them.
Record progress notes after each visit or phone contact (766.6(a)). Start discharge planning before discharge (766.2(a)(8)).

policies.title: RN Assessment, Reassessment, Patient/Caregiver Education and Medications and Treatments
state_specifics: An RN does the initial assessment before services start (766.3(b)) and reassesses at least every 6 months and on any change in condition.
Document medications and treatments in the plan of care. Reconcile them at each assessment.
Teach the patient and caregiver and document the teaching.
Medicaid clients get an annual independent assessment and practitioner order (18 NYCRR 505.14(b)).

policies.title: Plan of Care and Plan Updates
state_specifics: Build a plan for every patient from the RN's assessment (766.3(b)).

The plan covers: pertinent diagnosis and prognosis, any need for palliative care, mental and emotional status, frequency of each service, medications, treatments, diet, functional limitations and rehabilitation potential. Include therapy orders and the frequency and duration of all ordered services if applicable.
Review and revise the plan as often as needed and at least every 6 months. Document each review in the clinical record (766.3(d)(1)).
Promptly alert the authorized practitioner to significant changes (766.3(d)(2)).
For MLTC clients, the plan records the level, amount, frequency and duration the plan authorized.

policies.title: Medical Orders
state_specifics: Obtain an order from the patient's authorized practitioner for every patient. Authorized practitioners are an MD, DO, podiatrist, licensed midwife or nurse practitioner. Confirm the full text of 766.4 before finalizing.
Review and revise orders as needs change and at least every 6 months.
Orders reference diagnoses, medications, treatments, prognosis, palliative-care needs and other pertinent information.
The practitioner authenticates orders and changes, including telephone/verbal orders, within 12 months.
Verbal orders are taken only by an RN, read back, written and signed. Discharge needs 48 hours' notice to the practitioner (766.2(a)(9)).

policies.title: Aide Care Plan, Orientation to the Care Plan, Communication of Changes and Task Documentation
state_specifics: The RN prepares a written aide care plan from the plan of care. Before the first visit, the RN orients the aide to it.
The aide records tasks on the aide activity sheet at every visit. Sheets go in the clinical record (766.6(a)).
Aides report changes in condition, adverse reactions and problems with the home to the RN right away (766.5(b)).
The RN follows up on reported changes and notifies the practitioner. Aides may never change the care plan.

policies.title: Clinical Supervision of All Services and Paraprofessional Staff
state_specifics: The governing authority ensures enough trained supervisory staff (766.5(a)).
Supervision includes case review, in-home visits to direct and evaluate care, clinical consultation and consultation on policy.

Evidence of supervision: services delivered at planned times and frequencies; assignment by licensure, training and demonstrated skill; prompt charting and reporting of changes; plans revised as needed.
Aides are supervised 'as appropriate' by an RN (766.5(c)). Supervisory visit frequency is in SVC-10.
Provide clinical consultation, orientation and training for staff.

policies.title: RN In-Home Supervisory Visits of Aides
state_specifics: The RN supervisor makes an in-home visit at the initial aide service visit, or on a change in aide when the aide lacks documented training and experience in the tasks. The RN demonstrates and instructs, with return demonstration (766.5(d)(1)).
Visit at least every 6 months, and whenever the patient's condition, needs or environment change (766.5(d)(2)).

Medicaid personal care: RN supervisory visit at least every 90 days (18 NYCRR 505.14(f)). The local district or MLTC contract may set the frequency, so state it on the plan of care. Confirm the current (f) text.
Instruct the aide on required observations and review written reports (766.5(d)(3)).
Write a report of every supervisory visit with the aide present. OMIG guidance disallows claims with no RN visit within 120 days before the date of service.

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Level II aides may prompt and assist with self-administered medication but may not administer it (18 NYCRR 505.14(a)(5)(ii)(a)(10)).
The RN documents medications in the plan of care.
Aides record each assistance. They report missed doses, refusals and adverse reactions to the RN at once.
Aides never inject, adjust doses, or set up or fill medication organizers beyond what the RN has assessed and the plan permits.

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Schedule the same personnel for the same patient where possible (766.2(a)(3)).
Deliver services at the planned times and frequencies (766.5(b)).
Log every missed or late visit. The scheduler arranges coverage and tells the RN and the client.
Tell the MLTC plan about repeated missed visits.
24/7 coverage and the emergency plan keep care going during disruptions (766.9(c), (o)).

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
state_specifics: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care since 1/1/2021. The agency selects its own vendor (choice model); data goes to the NYS EVV Data Aggregator.
EVV captures date, location, service, people and start and end times.
Resolve EVV exceptions within the agency's set time. The scheduler documents manual edits with the reason.
Keep time and payment records (766.11(h)).

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Aides report changes right away to the RN. Call 911 first in a life-threatening emergency.
The RN promptly alerts the authorized practitioner and affected providers (766.3(d)(2)) and documents it.
The RN makes an in-home visit to evaluate and revise the plan after a change (766.5(d)(2)).
Complete an incident report if the event involves injury or harm (see SAF-02).

policies.title: Discharge Planning, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: Start the discharge plan before discharge (766.2(a)(8)). Aim for a safe, timely and appropriate discharge or transfer.
Notify the authorized practitioner at least 48 hours before discharge (766.2(a)(9)).
Consult the patient or caregiver and other professional staff about the discharge plan.
Write a discharge summary for the clinical record (766.6(a)(10)).
For Medicaid clients, notify the MLTC plan or district.

policies.title: Palliative Care and Life-Limiting Illness
state_specifics: Give patients with life-limiting conditions access to information and counseling.
Give access to palliative care consultation and services, including pain management, by referral.
Identify palliative care needs in the plan of care.
For patients who lack capacity, a legally authorized representative or health care proxy receives the information and decides (766.1(c)).

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs, MLTC Plans and Payers
state_specifics: MLTC plans authorize services, so the plan of care must match the authorization.
Plans may contract with 1 LHCSA per 100 enrollees downstate or per 60 rest of state. Exceptions: LHCSAExceptions@health.ny.gov.
CDPAP is handled by the Statewide Fiscal Intermediary, not the LHCSA.
Get rates, wage pass-through and billing terms in writing in each plan contract.
Medicaid-funded care downstate must meet wage parity (PHL §3614-c).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Patients have the right to be free from mistreatment and to be treated with dignity (766.1(a)(10)).
All staff report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation to the RN director at once. Call 911 if the client is in immediate danger.
The RN director reports to Adult Protective Services and law enforcement as required. Add the specific statutory reporting citations after counsel review.
Prohibit retaliation. Run the criminal history check and Registry check before hire.
Document in the incident record and the QI report.

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: Record accidents and incidents in the clinical record (766.6(a)(8)).
Staff report any incident to the RN director immediately, and the director files a written report within the agency's set time.
Notify the practitioner, family, MLTC plan and DOH as required.
Send incidents to the QI committee for review.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Apply Standard/Universal Precautions with every client.
Teach handwashing and supply-bag technique to nurses (nursing bag) and aides (aide bag technique).
Follow written procedures for storage, cleaning and disinfection of supplies and equipment (766.2(a)(5)).
Report communicable disease as required.
Occupational exposure control is in SAF-04.

policies.title: HIV and Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Control
state_specifics: Program covers barriers, training at hire and yearly, PPE, monitoring and an exposure-management procedure (766.11(l)).
Designate a person to receive exposure reports. Investigate every exposure.
Offer post-exposure testing, counseling and appropriate medical follow-up.
Keep HIV information confidential and disclose it only as law allows.
Monitor the prevention program. Definitions in 10 NYCRR 63.1/63.9 were not fetched, so confirm them.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness Plan, Patient Roster and Classification Levels
state_specifics: Keep a current written emergency plan and orient every employee to it (766.9(c)).
Address each type of emergency that could affect care (severe weather, power loss, pandemic, loss of facility).
Keep a patient roster: name, address, phone, emergency contact and health care proxy, classification level, Transportation Assistance Level, and ventilator or electricity dependence.
Assign each patient a classification level and Transportation Assistance Level at admission and review them at reassessment.
Verify patient contact information on a set schedule.

policies.title: Emergency Communications, Call-Down, Community Partners, Drills and Staff Training
state_specifics: Keep a staff call-down list and update it on a set schedule.
Have an alternate communication method if phones or internet are down.
Keep a contact list of the local health department, emergency management, EMS and law enforcement. Say how the agency answers their requests for information.
Take part in agency or community drills and exercises. Respond to DOH home care emergency response surveys through HCS.
Train staff on the plan at orientation and yearly, and after any revision. Staff know what to do when a patient refuses mandatory evacuation.

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: The RN checks the home environment at assessment and reports unsafe conditions (766.5(b)).
Staff may leave an unsafe situation and must report it to the RN director.
Provide training on violence prevention, ergonomics, and safe lifting and transfers.
Staff carry agency ID (766.2(a)(4)).

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Aides transport clients only if the plan of care authorizes it.
Use a valid license, insurance and a safe vehicle, with seatbelts and child/adaptive restraints.
Aides do not transport clients in their own vehicles unless the agency's insurance covers it.
Report accidents as incidents (SAF-02).
Mileage reimbursement follows wage policy.

policies.title: Personnel Policies, Qualifications, Job Descriptions and Performance Evaluations
state_specifics: Review personnel policies at least annually (766.11(a)).
Verify identity before hire. Verify employment history and references before patient contact. Verify licenses and credentials (766.11(e)-(f)).
Obtain a signed and dated application. Keep a written job description for each position (766.11(j)).
Do an annual performance assessment that includes at least one in-home observation visit where applicable (766.11(k)).
Employ at least one RN. All staff must be qualified for their assigned duties.

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications, Training Verification and Certification
state_specifics: A personal care aide needs a DOH-approved HHA program or the 40-hour PCA basic training (18 NYCRR 505.14(e)), finished within 3 months of hire per the research summary.
HHAs complete a basic HHA program or an approved equivalency exam (10 NYCRR 700.2).
Before assigning an aide, check the training materials against a DOH- or SED-approved program (DAL DHCBS 20-05) and review the Registry aide profile.
Meet the 766.11(b) qualification requirement.
Keep the certificate and verification in the personnel record.

policies.title: Home Care Worker Registry
state_specifics: Designate at least two individuals to access and enter registry data (Part 403.3(a)).
For aides trained on or after 9/25/2009, access the Registry before assignment. No services until posted.
Post employment information within 10 business days of the start date (403.5(a)(6)).
Update within 10 business days for worker-requested corrections and on termination.
Keep written policies implementing Part 403 (403.3(b)).

policies.title: Criminal History Record Check (CHRC) and Background Checks
state_specifics: Request a CHRC for every prospective employee covered by Part 402. Designate authorized persons.
An authorized person signs the DOH form, and the form and two sets of fingerprints go to DOH within 10 business days of taking the prints.
The applicant shows two IDs, one government-issued with signature and one with photo. Resubmit within 14 days after rejected prints.
Temporary approval is allowed pending results, with §402.4 supervision, and the supervision is documented.
Handle Hold in Abeyance, Pending and Final Determination letters under written procedure. Report terminations to DOH. Keep CHRC records confidential and separate.

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual In-Service Training
state_specifics: Orientation covers agency policies, HIV and bloodborne pathogen exposure plan, infection control and universal precautions, protective equipment, HIV confidentiality, HIPAA and the emergency plan.
In-service is at least 6 hours a year for PCAs and 12 for HHAs (766.11(i)).
Medicaid personal care adds 3 hours semiannually (18 NYCRR 505.14(e), per research summary).
Bloodborne pathogen training at hire and yearly (766.11(l)).
Document attendance and a competency check.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Assess health status before an employee assumes patient care duties (766.11(c)) and annually.
Obtain a statement that the person is free from impairment (including habituation or addiction to drugs or alcohol) that risks patients or interferes with duties.
Document rubella immunity, measles immunity if born on or after 1/1/1957, and influenza vaccination status.
TB risk assessment, symptom evaluation and TB test (skin test or blood assay) before employment and annually.
Keep health records separate and confidential (766.11(g)).

policies.title: Influenza Vaccination and Mask Requirement
state_specifics: Influenza season is as determined by the Commissioner.
Document the vaccination status of all personnel (766.11(d)).
Unvaccinated personnel with direct patient contact wear a surgical or procedure mask during flu season, with education and supervision.
The text of 10 NYCRR 2.59 was not fetched. Confirm it before quoting.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each file holds verifications, licenses, evaluations, employment dates and time and payment records (766.11(g)-(h)).
Keep health records separate and confidential.
Keep personnel records 3 years after separation (766.12(a)(3)).
Keep a listing of all personnel at the principal office.

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: Home care aide minimum wage (PHL §3614-f) is $19.65 NYC/Long Island/Westchester and $18.65 rest of state as of 1/1/2026. It rises to $20.00/$19.00 on 1/1/2027.
Wage parity (PHL §3614-c) applies to Medicaid work in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester. The benefit portion is $2.54 NYC or $1.67 elsewhere, with an annual certification and audited statement.
Keep wage parity records 10 years.
Pay overtime and travel time as required under FLSA home care rules.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Treat clients with respect and dignity (766.1(a)(10)).
Keep client information confidential.
Staff may not accept gifts, loans or financial involvement with clients.
Staff do not use client phones, cars or property, and keep personal relationships with clients professional.
Violations lead to discipline and may be reported.

policies.title: Patient Care Clinical Record
state_specifics: Each patient has a confidential record (766.6(a)).

Contents: identifying data, medical orders, nursing assessments, plan of care, signed and dated progress notes, RN supervisory reports, aide observations and activity sheets, accident/incident documentation, rights receipt, discharge summary.
Notify the practitioner of changes in condition and document it.
Safeguard records against loss or unauthorized access, and govern use, removal and release (766.6(e)).
Electronic records must be secure, confidential and printable on request (766.12(b)).

policies.title: Client Records Retention and Agency Closure
state_specifics: Keep patient records at least 6 years after discharge (766.6(b)).
For minors, keep until 6 years after discharge or 3 years after age 18, whichever is longer (766.6(c)).
If the agency closes, the governing authority arranges storage and access (766.6(d)).
Tell DOH in writing where the records are kept.

policies.title: Agency Records and Reports Retention
state_specifics: Keep at the principal office: license, certificate of incorporation or articles, partnership agreement, assumed-name certificate, patient-care contracts, governing-authority and QA bylaws, current policies, current patient roster, personnel list (766.12(a)(1)).
Keep governing authority and committee minutes, patient-care financial records, complaints/grievances and personnel records at least 3 years (see retention rules in 766.12(a)(3)).
Records may be hard copy or electronic, secured, and available to DOH on request.
Each year give DOH statistical summaries, plus ownership, shareholder, director and officer lists, and any SEC documents, if applicable (766.12(c)).

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Submit all records and reports DOH requires promptly (766.12(a)).
Weekly HERDS survey with census by licensed county: opens Tuesday 8:00 a.m., closes Thursday 2:00 p.m. (hcstatrpts@health.ny.gov).
Annual registration (PHL §3605-b). Cost reports when DOH requires them (PHL §3612).
Annual wage parity certification and audited statement if downstate Medicaid work applies.
Annual statistical and ownership reports (766.12(c)).

documents.title: LHCSA Applicant Worksheet
documents.form_number: None printed on the form (Division of Home and Community Based Services, 'FINAL: December 2016')
documents.issuer: NYS Department of Health, Division of Home and Community Based Services
documents.version: FINAL: December 2016. This is the version posted on the DOH 'Guidance Documents for LHCSA Applicants' page. I did not find a newer one.
documents.how_used: Primary checklist (doc 0). DOH says applicants 'should use this form as a guide to assess the completeness of the Policy and Procedure Manual', and that it 'must be submitted with the Policy and Procedure Manual'. A policy must be submitted for each service requested. The form has no item numbers, so the item_ids below are positional: a section code plus the order of the bullets in the document. Only sections that apply to a personal-care LHCSA are listed. Nursing is included because Review Tool Part A marks it as required for every LHCSA. Personal Care Aide is included. The Home Health Aide, therapy, social work, nutrition, homemaker, housekeeper, physician and medical-supply sections apply only if the agency is approved for those services, so I left them out.

documents.title: NYSDOH LHCSA P & P Review Tool PART A (Initial Review Tool)
documents.issuer: NYS Department of Health, Division of Home and Community Based Services
documents.how_used: Doc 1. This is the DOH initial-review checklist. It sets the minimum list of policies, the per-policy format elements, the per-service job description and P&P requirement, and the program materials that must come with the manual. Items are numbered A-1, A-2, and so on, in the document's order. The document itself has no numbering.

documents.title: NYSDOH LHCSA P & P Manual Review Tool PART B (regulation crosswalk)
documents.issuer: NYS Department of Health, Division of Home and Community Based Services
documents.how_used: Doc 2. The regional-office surveyor uses this tool. It copies the text of 10 NYCRR Parts 765, 766, 402 and 403 and grades each policy's statement, procedure and overall acceptability. The item_ids use the document's own regulation numbering. Only provisions that require written policies, procedures or plans, or that the agency must address in its policies, are listed. Text is condensed with '…'.

documents.title: Guidance for Developing Policies and Procedures for a Licensed Home Care Services Agency (LHCSA)
documents.issuer: NYS Department of Health, Office of Primary Care and Health Systems Management, Division of Home and Community Based Services
documents.how_used: Doc 3. This sets the submission rules and the required format of each policy. Those are summarised in 'notes' and in the G items. Attachment B is the sample index with a regulatory crosswalk. Attachment C lists the materials due before the pre-opening survey.

medications

the orders will be reviewed and revised at a minimum every 6 months

discharge planning
